docs.deployment:title: Deploying the Web app
docs.deployment:body: Serve existing assets normally and fall back to index.html for page requests. Trunk's SPA fallback is enabled for development. An application 404 page is rendered after the document loads; an HTTP 404 status requires server-side configuration.
docs.history:title: History on both platforms
docs.history:body: Native navigation stores locations in memory. Web uses pathname URLs and browser history. Search-only updates can push or replace an entry. Unknown paths map to the application's 404 page.
docs.parameters:title: Paths and search params
docs.parameters:body: PathPattern matches named segments and builds encoded paths. SearchParams handles duplicate keys and query encoding. The gallery uses typed component routes and the section query parameter for page navigation.
docs.typedroutes:title: Define typed routes
docs.typedroutes:body: egui_component_router is a separate workspace crate. Implement Route for your page enum; the same navigation API runs on native desktop and Web. The router does not depend on the UI library.
docs.fonts:title: Fonts that travel with your app
docs.fonts:body: Load embedded or asynchronously downloaded font bytes for portable native and Web typography. Apply font-manager updates before rendering each frame. Both native and Web galleries download their CJK fallback from GitHub after startup, with a progress toast and retry on failure.
docs.colormode:title: Light and dark
docs.colormode:body: UiTheme contains both modes. Select the active theme when rendering. This website's header switches modes for the entire application, including every live demo.
docs.brandcolors:title: Our brand palette
docs.brandcolors:body: The gallery uses #6B65F5 on white with #202124 text in light mode, and #8B85FF on #101318 with #F6F7FB text in dark mode. Configure these in examples/theme.json. Each color scale's required foreground sets text and icons on its solid colors, such as solid buttons and the switch knob. focus_ring sets the color and width of the keyboard focus indicator for every component.
docs.tokens:title: A shared set of tokens
docs.tokens:body: Themes hold semantic foreground and background colors, color scales, the focus ring, typography sizes, corner radii, and component sizing. Presets translate those tokens into component styles.
docs.compose:title: Compose with egui
docs.compose:body: Use egui layouts to arrange components. Cards, fields, and scroll areas accept rendering closures, so the composition remains in your hands.
docs.customize:title: Customize the details
docs.customize:body: Style values are ordinary Rust structs. Use builder methods for common changes or edit public fields for precise control. Styling stays local to the component.
docs.presets:title: Start with a preset
docs.presets:body: Style constructors give you a consistent baseline. Buttons include solid, surface, outline, and ghost variants, with multiple sizes and theme color palettes.
docs.nextsteps:title: Where to go next
docs.nextsteps:body: Explore the live component examples, then customize presets to match your product. Components work in both native eframe applications and WebAssembly applications.
docs.firstcomponent:title: Your first component
docs.firstcomponent:body: Pick a style preset and render directly into your Ui. Every component returns or exposes the interaction state you need to connect it to your application.
docs.theme:title: Load a theme
docs.theme:body: Load your theme JSON once when the application starts. The gallery's examples/theme.json contains a complete light and dark theme you can use as a starting point.
docs.installation:title: Installation
docs.installation:body: Add egui_component to an existing egui application. Components render inside your current Ui; there is no application framework to adopt.

ecml.setup:title: Set up a view
ecml.setup:body: Experimental markup for egui_component interfaces. Templates describe the UI; Rust owns the state and behavior. Every demo in this guide is editable and re-renders as you type. Enable the ecml feature, register the values and handlers a template may use, then load a template source. Keep the View and your state in the application rather than recreating them each frame, and call show once per pass from any egui host. ECML does not create windows or depend on eframe.
ecml.bindings:title: Bind state and handle events
ecml.bindings:body: model exposes a readable and writable value: its getter returns the value, cloning a field or computing one, and its setter receives an owned value. A computed model such as "all done" can set every row in its setter. bind exposes a read-only value or calculation. on registers a synchronous handler receiving the state. Supported value types are String, bool, i32 and i64. Templates reach nothing that is not registered, and calculations belong in bind getters rather than template expressions. Edits write back while drawing; click handlers run after the traversal and see those edits. All ECML demos share the state below, so the name you type appears in every demo.
ecml.syntax:title: Syntax rules
ecml.syntax:body: A template has exactly one root element. Attribute values are always quoted, except the bare e-else, and elements are closed with a closing tag or />. Component tags match their Rust module names, such as text_edit, and layout and fragment are built in. Directives use e-, dynamic attributes use a colon and events use @. Structured attributes use dotted paths such as item_spacing.x. Comments are allowed inside elements, and the entities amp, lt, gt, quot and apos are supported. Unknown tags, attributes or names and type mismatches are errors, never silently ignored. Templates are limited to 256 KiB and 64 levels.
ecml.loops:title: Lists with e-for
ecml.loops:body: e-for="todo in todos" repeats an element once per row of a list registered with .list in Rust, and is allowed on any element except the root. The read accessor returns an iterator, so filtering and sorting stay in Rust. Rows are identified by a key from Rust rather than by position, so focus and edits follow a row when rows are added, removed or reordered. Inside the loop, todo.name reaches only the row's own registrations, and row events are written @click="todo.remove"; the handler receives that row's key. Model edits inside a loop are applied when the loop finishes, so later controls in the same row show the new value on the next pass. Only the first row with each key is shown, and duplicates are reported. Lists can also nest; see Nested lists. Give the e-for element an explicit id so focus inside rows survives template edits.
ecml.nestedLoops:title: Nested lists
ecml.nestedLoops:body: Lists can nest without reflection. A row registers a child list with .list on its row builder, and e-for="task in project.tasks" resolves project.tasks to that registration, just as project.name resolves to a row binding. The child read accessor receives the parent row, and its lookup searches the mutable parent row, so writes are located level by level. Row handlers of child rows receive the key path, here (project name, task id). Inner loops can still use outer aliases, and an inner alias must differ from outer ones. Writes anywhere inside the outermost loop are applied when it finishes, and duplicate keys are checked within one parent row.
ecml.conditionals:title: Conditionals
ecml.conditionals:body: e-if="name" draws an element only while a registered bool is true; e-else-if and e-else directly follow it as siblings and form a chain that draws at most its first true branch. Conditions take one name, root or alias.name, optionally negated with !, like :disabled; anything more belongs in a Rust bind getter. e-else is the only attribute written without a value. A hidden branch draws nothing and takes no space, and switching branches does not disturb the identity of other elements. Outside loops a condition sees earlier edits in the same pass; inside loops it sees them on the next pass. e-if cannot share an element with e-for: nest them, and filter rows in Rust. To show several elements under one condition, wrap them in a fragment.
ecml.styling:title: Dynamic styling
ecml.styling:body: Styling attributes take a constant or, with a colon, an expression. A constant is a word, as in variant="ghost", or a theme path, as in color="$theme.colors.gray.l6". $theme is reserved: its paths mirror the Rust Theme fields ($theme.colors.<scale>.<foreground|l0..l9>, $theme.colors.<bg|fg>.<base|subtle|accent>, and $theme.colors.<scale> where a whole scale is wanted) and are checked when the template compiles; nothing is reflected. In a :attribute, words are quoted and the value can be chosen with cond ? value : value, where cond is a registered bool, optionally negated with !. Conditions chain, as in :variant="a ? 'solid' : b ? 'surface' : 'ghost'", and the first true one wins. Bool attributes such as :strikethrough take a condition directly. There is no arithmetic, comparison or function call: compute in a Rust bind getter. A constant and its :attribute cannot be combined on one element.
ecml.text:title: Text and interpolation
ecml.text:body: text accepts size="md" (default) or size="heading". Double-brace interpolation displays any registered model or binding. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; whitespace inside the text is preserved. color takes a theme color such as $theme.colors.gray.l6 (default: the text color), and underline and strikethrough draw a 1-point line in the text color. All of them also work as :size, :color, :underline and :strikethrough; see Dynamic styling.
ecml.button:title: Buttons
ecml.button:body: button accepts size (xs, sm, md, lg), variant (solid, surface, outline, ghost), width, disabled and @click. :disabled reads a registered bool and may be negated with !. A literal disabled="true" cannot be combined with :disabled. color takes a color scale such as $theme.colors.red (default: primary). size, variant and color also work as :size, :variant and :color; see Dynamic styling. Labels support interpolation.
ecml.textEdit:title: Text inputs
ecml.textEdit:body: text_edit edits a String model through e-model and accepts size, variant (subtle, outline, flushed), width, placeholder, disabled and :disabled; size and variant also work as :size and :variant. Placeholders support interpolation. Without a width, a text_edit uses the available width. It also supports @submit, @cancel, @blur and autofocus; see Text input events. Give editable controls an explicit id so focus and cursor survive template edits.
ecml.textEvents:title: Text input events
ecml.textEvents:body: A focused text_edit fires one event whenever it loses focus: @submit for Enter, @cancel for Escape, and @blur for anything else, such as a click elsewhere or Tab. If the specific handler is not registered, @blur fires instead, so @submit="save" @blur="save" saves exactly once. Handlers take no arguments and may be row handlers such as todo.save; they run after drawing, once per frame, and see the text typed in the same frame. A field with @submit keeps focus after Enter so the next entry can be typed straight away. autofocus="true" focuses a field when it appears: on the first show, when its e-if branch is chosen, or when its row is added. Disabled fields fire no events. Multiline input is not available in ECML yet.
ecml.switch:title: Switches
ecml.switch:body: switch edits a bool model through e-model and accepts size (sm, md, lg) or :size, disabled and :disabled.
ecml.checkbox:title: Checkboxes
ecml.checkbox:body: checkbox edits a bool model through e-model and accepts size (sm, md, lg) or :size, disabled and :disabled. Text content becomes its label and supports interpolation; without content only the box is drawn.
ecml.layout:title: Layout
ecml.layout:body: layout maps directly to egui. direction is top_down (default) or left_to_right. cross_align is min (default), center or max. item_spacing.x and item_spacing.y are nonnegative logical points; unspecified axes inherit from the parent Ui, and overrides affect only the layout and its descendants. Horizontal layouts start at one control's height and grow with content. Layout does not stretch, scroll, clip or wrap children. Only layout and fragment accept child elements.
ecml.fragment:title: Fragments
ecml.fragment:body: fragment groups elements without creating a layout: its children are drawn straight into the parent, inheriting its direction and spacing, so a fragment inside a horizontal layout keeps its children in the row. Use it to apply e-if, e-else-if, e-else or e-for to several elements at once. It accepts only id and those directives, and no text. A fragment may also be the root, letting a template draw several top-level elements. There is no <> shorthand.
ecml.sources:title: Sources and hot reload
ecml.sources:body: The source macro resolves paths relative to the calling crate's Cargo.toml. Native builds with debug assertions read the file and reload it about every 150 ms after you save; release and WASM builds embed the text at compile time. Templates are validated when loaded, and a replacement is applied at the next frame boundary while state and handlers are kept. Changes to Rust code or registrations still require a rebuild.
ecml.diagnostics:title: Identity and diagnostics
ecml.diagnostics:body: load returns an error for an invalid initial template. An invalid replacement keeps the last valid interface and reports the file, line, column and reason through last_error, and through a floating window unless it is disabled. A valid replacement clears the error. Explicit ids must be unique within a View; controls with ids keep their focus and editing state when moved, while automatic ids may change with structure. Use one View per mounted location. Try breaking any demo template to see the error.
ecml:editHint: Edit the template; valid changes render immediately without losing state.
